page.metodoloji.title: Methodology
page.metodoloji.lede: WebKarne passively measures a domain's public security configuration and turns it into a plain-language report card that needs no technical background. Here is how the measurement works.
page.metodoloji.s1.body:
WebKarne makes only DNS queries and ordinary HTTP GET requests — exactly what a browser or a mail server would do.

No attack, vulnerability scan, directory/file probing, port scan, login attempt or form submission is ever performed. A timeout and a rate limit are mandatory on every request. The measurement is limited to publicly available information that needs no permission from the site owner.
page.metodoloji.s2.body:
The report card has four dimensions: Email and domain identity (SPF, DKIM, DMARC, DNSSEC, DANE, MTA-STS and the like); Transport and server security (HTTPS, TLS versions, certificate, HSTS, security headers); Privacy and tracking; Technology and attack surface.

The first two dimensions are measured today. The collectors for privacy and tracking, and for technology and attack surface, are under development; until they are ready these dimensions are shown honestly as not measured.
page.metodoloji.s3.body:
A collector records exactly what it observed as raw data; it never judges good or bad, and never assigns a score.

Scoring is a completely separate layer that runs on versioned rules. This means the same raw data can be re-scored later even if the rules change. Every dimension grade on the card states which ruleset version produced it.
page.metodoloji.s4.body:
Every control is shown in one of four states: passed, failed, could not measure, and not applicable.

Could-not-measure never means no record. If a query fails, it is recorded as could-not-measure without being confused with the record being absent; a domain that does not exist at all (NXDOMAIN) is kept distinct from a query error. This distinction is critical to the accuracy of the measurement.
page.metodoloji.s5.body:
Letter grades and their thresholds live in a versioned configuration file, separate from the code. Every dimension grade you see on a card comes from that configuration.

This keeps the grade scale transparent and auditable; why a grade was given can be traced all the way back to the raw data and the ruleset version.
page.metodoloji.s6.body:
WebKarne measures only public configuration; it does not access a site's content, user data or private information. Nothing that is not measured is ever guessed or fabricated — if it was not measured, it is shown as such.

This report is a snapshot of public configuration, not a security audit. A good grade does not guarantee a site is secure in every respect; a weak grade rests on concrete, observed gaps.
page.hakkinda.title: About
page.hakkinda.lede: WebKarne is an open research project that measures the digital security posture of domains in Türkiye.
page.hakkinda.s1.body:
To make a domain's security configuration understandable without requiring technical expertise. Measurements are designed to be measurable, reproducible and explainable.

The goal is not to shame a site, but to give its owners and users concrete, fixable information.
page.hakkinda.s2.body:
WebKarne is part of a thesis project. It develops and applies a consistent method for measuring domain security across a Türkiye sample.

Method decisions and measurement rules are documented; findings are recorded so they can be reproduced.
page.hakkinda.s3.body:
All measurement is passive and relies only on publicly available data. No attack, unauthorized access or intrusive probing is ever performed.

Every request honours a timeout and a rate limit; measurement is carried out so as not to burden the systems being measured.
page.hakkinda.s4.body:
The measurement code and method are open; anyone can inspect how we measure. Transparency is the basis of trust in the results.

Raw data is retained and the method is documented; the details are on the Open Data and Methodology pages.
page.acik-veri.title: Open Data
page.acik-veri.lede: Raw data is retained and the method is open so that measurements can be reproduced.
page.acik-veri.s1.body:
The study is built on a sample frame of domains belonging to Türkiye. Domains are marked with sector labels: bank, university, public body, municipality, hospital, e-commerce and media.

Building and expanding the sample frame is ongoing; this page will be updated as the scope becomes clearer.
page.acik-veri.s2.body:
Every scan is a new record; raw data is never deleted or overwritten. This means a measurement can later be re-scored or examined from a different angle.

This is a foundational rule for preserving the scientific validity of the measurement.
page.acik-veri.s3.body:
The dataset and export tools will be announced here once they are ready to publish.

The aim is to make the raw measurements and the method accessible so that findings can be independently verified.
page.acik-veri.s4.body:
How the data is collected, which controls are measured and how grades are computed is described in detail on the Methodology page.

Every grade can be traced back to the ruleset version that produced it and the raw data it rests on.
page.sektor.title: Sector Analyses
page.sektor.lede: Comparative analyses across sectors are being prepared.
page.sektor.s1.body:
We are working on analyses that compare a domain's grade with its own sector — banks, universities, public bodies, municipalities, hospitals, e-commerce and media.

This section will show sector distributions and comparative charts once enough measurements have accumulated.
page.sektor.s2.body: To see the detailed report card for a single domain, run a query from the home page. You can find how the measurement works on the Methodology page.

finding.EMAIL_DMARC_POLICY_NONE.title: DMARC policy is not protective enough
finding.EMAIL_DMARC_POLICY_NONE.summary: A DMARC record exists but is configured as p=none.
finding.EMAIL_DMARC_POLICY_NONE.meaning: DMARC helps determine whether email sent in your domain's name really belongs to you. Your current setting (p=none) only reports; it does not stop spoofed email from reaching recipients.
finding.EMAIL_DMARC_POLICY_NONE.info: This setting does not put your domain directly at risk, but in phishing attacks spoofed email can be sent in your name.
finding.EMAIL_DMARC_POLICY_NONE.fix: For stronger protection, once you are sure your domain is ready, raise the policy first to p=quarantine and then to p=reject.
finding.EMAIL_DMARC_POLICY_NONE.fix_succ: A correctly configured DMARC record protects your domain's reputation and largely blocks spoofed email.
finding.EMAIL_SPF_SOFTFAIL.title: SPF does not hard-fail unauthorized senders
finding.EMAIL_NO_MTA_STS.title: No MTA-STS policy found
finding.EMAIL_NO_MTA_STS.summary: No enforced-encryption policy is defined for mail transport.
finding.EMAIL_NO_TLS_RPT.title: TLS-RPT reporting is not defined
finding.EMAIL_NO_TLS_RPT.summary: There is no reporting address for mail-transport problems.
finding.EMAIL_DKIM_NOT_OBSERVED.title: DKIM record could not be observed
finding.EMAIL_DKIM_NOT_OBSERVED.summary: No DKIM key was found on common selectors; this does not mean “absent”.
finding.TRANSPORT_NO_HSTS.title: HSTS is not enabled
finding.TRANSPORT_NO_HSTS.summary: Your website does not use HTTP Strict Transport Security.
finding.TRANSPORT_MISSING_SECURITY_HEADE: One or more of the four core security headers is absent.
finding.TRANSPORT_NO_SECURITY_TXT.title: security.txt not found
finding.EMAIL_SPF_SOFTFAIL.meaning: SPF states which servers may send mail in your domain's name. Because your record ends with ~all (softfail), unauthorized senders are not firmly rejected; many recipients will still accept such mail.
finding.EMAIL_SPF_SOFTFAIL.fix: Once every legitimate source that sends mail for your domain is listed in the SPF record, change the terminator from ~all to -all, so unauthorized senders are firmly rejected.
finding.EMAIL_NO_MTA_STS.meaning: MTA-STS requires sending mail servers to connect to you over encryption. Without it, an attacker in the middle can try to downgrade encryption.
finding.EMAIL_NO_MTA_STS.fix: Publish an MTA-STS policy file (/.well-known/mta-sts.txt) and add the _mta-sts TXT record. Start with mode=testing, monitor, then move to mode=enforce.
finding.EMAIL_NO_TLS_RPT.meaning: TLS-RPT lets encryption problems in mail transport be reported back to you. Without it, you cannot see those problems.
finding.EMAIL_NO_TLS_RPT.fix: Add a _smtp._tls TXT record defining an address for reports (e.g. rua=mailto:tlsrpt@yourdomain).
finding.EMAIL_DKIM_NOT_OBSERVED.meaning: DKIM selector names cannot be discovered from DNS, only guessed. Not finding a record on common selectors does not mean DKIM is absent; this is a method limitation.
finding.EMAIL_DKIM_NOT_OBSERVED.fix: If you know the DKIM selector your mail provider uses, you can verify it directly. This observation does not lower your score.
finding.TRANSPORT_NO_HSTS.meaning: HSTS tells browsers to reach the site only over HTTPS. Without it, the first visit can be hijacked over an unencrypted connection.
finding.TRANSPORT_NO_HSTS.fix: Add the Strict-Transport-Security header; a max-age of at least 180 days is recommended (e.g. max-age=15552000; includeSubDomains).
finding.TRANSPORT_MISSING_SECURITY_HEADE: The core security headers steer the browser against common attacks (content injection, clickjacking, type sniffing). When they are missing, those protections are not in effect.
Add the missing headers: content-security-policy, x-frame-options, x-content-type-options and referrer-policy.
finding.TRANSPORT_NO_SECURITY_TXT.meanin: security.txt is a standard file that tells security researchers how to report a vulnerability to you. It is a maturity signal.
finding.TRANSPORT_NO_SECURITY_TXT.fix: Publish a /.well-known/security.txt file; at minimum it should include a valid Contact field.
